narration: Observe this mass on a spring... If it pulls harder the more it stretches, why isn't its acceleration constant? Let us reason together!
Most imagine acceleration stays steady... But wait! As the spring pulls the block back toward the center, the stretch shrinks. Less stretch means less force!
Here is the profound truth—Force equals negative k times x! Acceleration continuously varies, reaching absolute zero right at the mean equilibrium position!
And behold! Zero force at the center means zero acceleration—yet maximum speed! Nature is truly wondrous. Test your newfound mastery in the quiz below!
